questions.q: Once a prompt is tokenized, what is the primary function of a base (foundation) LLM?
options: To predict the next token in the sequence
To search the internet
To check facts against a database
To translate the prompt into code
questions.explain: Base models complete text token by token; instruction tuning makes them follow requests.
questions.evidence: the primary function of the "Base LLM" (or Foundation model) is to predict the token in that sequence.

questions.q: Besides giving examples, which technique uses primary content to steer the model?
options: Raising the temperature
Asking the same question twice
Providing cues rather than examples
Writing the prompt in capital letters
questions.explain: A cue (for example the start of the desired output) nudges the model toward the format you want.
questions.evidence: Another technique for using primary content is to provide cues rather than examples.

questions.q: What does the quality of results from a prompt depend on?
options: Only on which model you use
How much information you provide and how well-crafted the prompt is
The time of day
How long you wait before sending it
questions.explain: Instructions, context, inputs and examples all improve results.
questions.evidence: the quality of results depends on how much information you provide it and how well-crafted the prompt is.

options: The most popular prompt template
The maximum number of tokens in a reply
A ranking of the best models
A sampling technique (nucleus sampling) that controls how deterministic the model is
questions.explain: Lower Top P (or temperature) gives more deterministic, factual answers; higher gives more varied ones.
questions.evidence: Top P - A sampling technique with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where you can control how deterministic the model is.

questions.q: What does the guide recommend about the context you give in a prompt?
options: The more specific and relevant to the task, the better
Always keep it under ten words
Leave it out so the model can be creative
Use the same context for every task
questions.explain: Specific, relevant detail matters most when you want a particular outcome or style.
questions.evidence: Usually, the more specific and relevant the context is to the task you are trying to perform, the better.

questions.q: Why is prompting described as an 'emergent property' of an LLM?
options: Because prompts only work in emergencies
Because the model was explicitly programmed to follow prompts
Because it is not a feature built into the model but something we discover as we use it
Because prompts are generated by the model itself
questions.explain: That is why prompt techniques are found by experimentation.
questions.evidence: prompting is an emergent property of an LLM meaning that this is not a feature that is built into the model but rather something we discover as we use the model.

options: A prompt that has zero words
A prompt with no examples or demonstrations
A prompt that is sent without an API key
A prompt that always gets a wrong answer
questions.explain: Few-shot prompting adds a handful of examples; zero-shot relies on instructions alone.
questions.evidence: Zero-shot prompting means that the prompt used to interact with the model won't contain examples or demonstrations.

questions.q: Chain-of-thought prompting can be combined with which technique to do better on complex reasoning tasks?
options: Prompt injection
Lowering the token limit
Asking for one-word answers
Few-shot prompting
questions.explain: Worked examples that show their reasoning help the model reason step by step.
questions.evidence: You can combine it with few-shot prompting to get better results on more complex tasks that require reasoning before responding.

options: A task is split into subtasks, and each response is used as input to the next prompt
The same prompt is sent many times and the answers are averaged
Several users write one prompt together
The model is asked to ignore its earlier answers
questions.explain: Breaking work into steps makes LLM pipelines more reliable and easier to debug.
questions.evidence: Once those subtasks have been identified, the LLM is prompted with a subtask and then its response is used as input to another prompt.

questions.q: Why is it important to protect against prompt attacks such as prompt injection?
options: They make responses slower
They increase API costs
They could bypass safety guardrails and break the model's guiding principles
They change the model's language
questions.explain: User input is mixed with your instructions, so untrusted text can try to override them.
questions.evidence: it's really important to protect against prompt attacks that could bypass safety guardrails and break the guiding principles of the model.
